purpose: Model a finite-speed threshold cascade on a coarse-grained network as a falsifiable laboratory for domino/mousetrap-style gravitational-structural triggering hypotheses.

analogy_boundary.domino: topology of sequential threshold crossing only
analogy_boundary.mousetrap_ping_pong: a small seed can unlock pre-stored local reservoirs; the seed does not supply the total released energy
analogy_boundary.nuclear_fission: chain-reaction topology analogy only; no claim that gravity has a fission-like self-reproducing microscopic reaction
analogy_boundary.cosmic_web: may be represented as a graph of coarse-grained structures; graph topology is not proof of causal triggering

hard_invariants: released cascade energy is traced to local pre-existing reservoirs plus external seed
TOKEN_VAZIO is not zero and is never promoted to evidence
branching_potential > 1 is not a proof of a physical avalanche

activation_rule.equation: Q_i(t)=sum incoming pulses; activate if Q_i >= Theta_i

promotion_requirements: derive threshold from a physical instability or transition
derive reservoir from a bounded physical energy budget
derive coupling from GR/MHD/radiative physics rather than fit it freely
map propagation channel and attenuation to a source-specific model
define at least one observable signature distinguishable from independent coincident events
run null models with randomized topology and event times
quantify selection effects and observational cadence
claim_boundary: This implementation demonstrates a causal threshold-cascade computation. It does not demonstrate that the Universe, the cosmic web, stars, black holes or gravitational fields undergo such an avalanche.
